analysis.title: APAC Tech Views: SpaceX Q326 implications: Substantial capex upgrade to accelerate its build-out
key_insights: SpaceX Q3 2026 sales grew 87% QoQ and 161% YoY to US$14.6bn, above the Street's US$12.9bn. Superintelligence (SI) was US$7.56bn (+195% QoQ), connectivity US$5.25bn (+29% QoQ) and space US$1.77bn (+104% QoQ). The share price rose 8% after hours.

Operating income swung from a net loss to a US$2.8bn gain. AI operating margin improved from -207% in Q325 and -49% in Q226 to positive 6% as cloud services ramp. Management called the quarter an inflection point.
Starlink subscribers grew from 12.0mn to 13.6mn. Monthly consumer ARPU rose 5% QoQ to US$69.

SI solutions/infrastructure revenue ramped from US$2.2bn to US$7.0bn (US$608mn from adding Cursor), with most of the rest from cloud. Backlog rose to US$63bn. ARR is projected to reach US$100bn by year-end (US$8.3bn monthly run rate) and US$500bn to US$1trn exiting 2027.
Management says cloud capex now pays back in under a year, and in some cases in 6 months, as compute stays very tight and the value of a GW of compute rises with model intelligence.
Grok Bot agentic platform, launched in August, has 800k paid weekly users. Grok Enterprise is above a US$1mn run rate (+50% QoQ).

Installed compute grew from 1.4GW to 1.7GW QoQ in Q326. The year-end target was raised from >2GW to 2.5-3GW. For 2027 the target adds a further 10GW to exit at 12.5-13GW, up from a prior 10GW. Musk cited turbine blades and vanes plus renewable sources to scale power and cooling by 10GW in 2027, with a stretch target of 20GW.

SpaceX deploys mainly on NVIDIA: 300MW in Q326 (about 2k GB300 racks) and a target of another 600k in Q426 (8.3k racks, about 1.3GW). For 2027 it expects 200k/month, upgrading to NVIDIA's Vera platform. UBS computes 2.4mn Vera would be about 33k racks and 8.2GW at 227kW and 1.10 PUE, costing US$260-300bn for compute and US$350bn including networking and data centers.

Q3 capex was US$19.6bn versus US$18.1bn expected (US$16.4bn AI, US$1.5bn connectivity, US$1.6bn space). Q4 capex guidance was raised to US$35-40bn versus a prior Street US$19.8bn. UBS raised SpaceX capex for 2026-27 from US$56bn/US$124bn to US$73bn/US$310bn.

SpaceX exited Q3 with US$90bn cash and US$39bn debt. ROIC improved from -3.6% to 10.7%. It plans to keep an investment grade rating for debt financing. UBS estimates 2027 operating cash flow of US$125bn (from US$28bn), requiring US$170bn of financing cash flow and US$67bn from cash on hand.

Terafab targets initial production in H228 at its Texas site, to support an SI compute need of 1TW. The initial process is based on Intel's and it is in talks with TSMC. UBS says it needs a couple of years to start and more to disrupt.

UBS expects SpaceX commentary to lift AI supply chain sentiment. Constrained compute, rising compute value and 6-12 month cloud payback support the expansion. Neo Clouds would need to raise pricing on new contracts, find new capital including from chip companies, or pare back lower-return projects.

SpaceX plans about 8k racks in Q4 (from about 2k in Q3), and 33k Vera racks in 2027. That equals 35% of UBS's 95k NVIDIA rack estimate, with upside if other hyperscalers follow. UBS CoWoS/HBM forecasts support up to 125k racks. Power is the key constraint: UBS base case rises from 26GW to 51GW (57GW including general servers).

Super Micro rose 16% after hours after raising its Sep quarter revenue outlook from US$14.5-15.5bn to US$18.5bn and gross margin from 10.4-10.8% to 12-12.5%. SpaceX suppliers include Wistron (L10 rack assembly for Dell) and Supermicro, with Hon Hai and Pegatron coming in.

Beneficiaries of the NVIDIA ramp in Asia include TSMC, ASE, KYEC, Chroma, Hon Precision, Advantest, Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, Ibiden, Unimicron, Victory Giant, Delta and Lite-On. The SoW Dojo project has rack assembly at Wistron and fabrication at TSMC, with design service possibly shifting to MediaTek.

Management expects weekly Starship flights in 1H27 and possibly twice-weekly in 2H27, implying up to 72 flights in 2027 (UBSe 30, Street 40). WIN Semi is a key beneficiary: UBS expects LEO revenue to rise from 10% of sales in 2026 to 30% by 2028, and gross margin to rise from 29% this year to over 37% by 2028.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 beat on sales and profitability, with a raised compute deployment plan. Shares rose 8% after hours from a US$147.79 close. UBS analyst John Hodulik raised 2026-27 capex estimates.
Shares rose 16% after hours after Supermicro raised its Sep quarter revenue outlook to US$18.5bn and gross margin to 12-12.5%. UBS names it a SpaceX supplier.
Foundry for the NVIDIA chain that SpaceX commits to for most of its ramp.
Primary memory supplier to the NVIDIA-related chain that benefits from SpaceX rack deployments.
Appears in the company disclosures table as a UBS Buy. The text does not discuss AMD.
WIN Semiconductors (3105.TWO, no US listing) is a key beneficiary of Starship flights. UBS raised estimates and expects LEO revenue to reach 30% of sales by 2028.
Wistron supplies L10 rack assembly and is a SpaceX supplier.
Hon Hai Precision is a new ODM entrant to the SpaceX supply chain.
Pegatron is a new ODM entrant to the SpaceX supply chain.
